# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

# Repository Report: /app (transaction-enrichment-python)

## 1. Overall Structure

**Language / stack:** Python 3.9, Flask web service, heavy use of pandas/numpy vectorized rule engines (`np.select` over lists of `[condition, choice]` pairs). Fuzzy matching via `fuzzywuzzy`/`python-Levenshtein`, clustering via `scipy`/`scikit-learn`.

**Layout:**
```
/app
├── Dockerfile                                 # python:3.9.2 base; pip install -e .; gunicorn on port 9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                               # package deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, scipy, sklearn...
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                        # Flask app creation, request timing logging (lines 7-28)
        ├── Controller.py                      # HTTP endpoints + per-bank orchestration (936 lines)
        ├── BankScripts/                       # 32 bank-specific categorizers (Axis, HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Kotak, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/                    # shared enrichment pipeline + regex dictionaries
```

**Build/run:** No requirements.txt (deps in `setup.py`). Docker: `pip3 install -e .` then `gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (Dockerfile lines 7–11). Dev mode: `app.run(port=9898)` in `__init__.py:31`.

**API (Controller.py):**
- `GET /` — health check (line 51)
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` (line 55) — clusters transactions by partyName similarity
- `POST /categorizeTransaction` (line 69) — main entry. Payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`. A giant if/elif per bank (lines 91–932), each executing the same pipeline: bank categorizer → (if CREDIT_CARD: `card_clean_names` + `card_purpose`) → `purpose` → `clean_names` → `internal_payment` (if accountHolder given) → `salary_detection` (if SAVING) → `pfm_categorization` + `simple_description` (if PFM enabled).

**Enrichment output columns:** `transactionCategory` (category), `transactionSubcategory` (sub-tag), `partyName`/`party2` (payee/counterparty), `merchantType`, `isInternalPayment`, `pfmCategoryOne/Two/Type`, `pfmSimpleDescription`, `Group_ID`.

## 2. Enrichment / Labeling Logic

### Bank-specific categorizers — `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` (32 files)
Each exposes one function `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` (a few also take `accountHolder`: BankOfMaharashtra, CityUnion, UCO). All follow the HDFC pattern (representative example, `HDFC.py`, 277 lines):

- **Category assignment** (`transactionCategory`), lines 11–104: ordered regex rules on `description` + `type` + `amount`, default `"TRANSFER"`. Includes:
  - **Reversal/bounce detection:** `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` (line 21), `UPI_REVERSAL` (22), `IMPS_REVERSAL` (23), `ATM_REVERSAL` (24), generic `REVERSAL` (25), `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` (27), `NEFT_RETURN`/`RTGS_RETURN` (28–29), `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY` (30), `CHEQUE_RETURN` (69–72); pairwise-row heuristics — same amount debit-then-credit ⇒ `REVERSAL`/`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` (lines 98–99)
  - **Cheque detection:** `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL` (50), `CHEQUE_PAID` (71, 74), `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` (73, 75, 100 — 15-digit remark heuristic)
  - Transfers/rails: `TPT` (57), `UPI` (58), `IMPS` (59), `NEFT` (60), `RTGS` (61), `FUND_TRANSFER` (96)
- **Subcategory assignment**, lines 112–132: `SALARY` (119, 124), `SALARY_DISBURSED` (125), `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` — cheque bounce when prior balance < 0 (line 126), `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` via "SELF" (127), `LOAN`/`LOAN_REPAYMENT`/`INVESTMENT`/`CREDIT_CARD_PAYMENT` etc.
- **Payee extraction** (`partyName`), lines 146–275: positional token extraction (`sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_colon`, ...) and regex `py_extract` per rail — UPI/IMPS/NEFT counterparties (147–163), POS merchant (164–165), auto-pay biller (169–174), payment-gateway merchant (176–179), cheque payee via `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` (188–197), transfer counterparty via `HDFC_FT_PATTERN*`/`FT_PATTERN*` (200–215), salary stop-word cleanup (217, 234–235), plus post-cleaning passes (225–273) and `party2` (space-stripped name, line 275).

Other bank files (all same shape, largest listed): `Kotak.py` (327), `HDFC.py` (276), `Indusind.py` (263), `IDBI.py` (247), `ICICI.py` (245), `BankOfMaharashtra.py` (235), `StandardCharted.py` (208), `Canara.py` (201), `SBI.py` (193), `PNB.py` (192), `Axis.py` (188), down to `SVC.py` (68).

### Cross-bank utility scripts — `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/`

| File | Function (line) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Purpose.py` | `purpose(transactions, accountType)` (line 9) | Main sub-tag engine for savings/current: SALARY detection by regex (14–17), INSURANCE_CLAIM, LOAN/LOAN_REPAYMENT (23–46), CREDIT_CARD_PAYMENT (48), spend tags (FUEL, TRAVEL, FOOD, E_COMMERCE, UTILITY_BILL, RENT... lines 56–148), **bounce classification** `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`/`INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` on cheque returns (145–147), INTERNAL_PAYMENT (148); category overrides TDS/TAX_REFUND/REFUND/CASHBACK (154–170); merchantType assignment (NBFC, HFC, Streaming, Groceries... 182–298) |
| `CleanName.py` (1971 lines) | `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` (line 9) | Massive payee-normalization dictionary: maps raw partyName/description to canonical merchant names (DTH, broadband, electricity boards, etc.), thousands of regex→name rules |
| `CardPurpose.py` | `card_purpose(transactions)` (line 9) | Credit-card sub-tags (LOAN_REPAYMENT, TRAVEL, FOOD, GST via `TAX_CC`... lines 12–72) and CC merchantType (77–157) |
| `CardCleanNames.py` (927 lines) | `card_clean_names(transactions)` (line 9) | Credit-card merchant/payee name normalization |
| `SalaryDetection.py` | `salary_detection(transactions)` (line 16) | Statistical salary detection: Levenshtein-distance clustering of partyName into `Group_ID` (25–34); excludes reversals/returns/deposits/loans (37–53); Scenario 1 (no salary yet): mode-amount and name-frequency heuristics (64–110); Scenario 2: propagate salary across group, second-salary detection, REIMBURSEMENT reassignment (<30% of max salary) (116–210) |
| `InternalPayment.py` | `internal_payment(transactions, accountHolder, bank, accountType)` (line 8) | Self-transfer detection: strips honorifics/corporate suffixes (line 10), fuzzy-matches partyName vs account holder (`fuzzy_match`, threshold 75) for transfer-type categories (15, 20–53); sets `isInternalPayment` flag (55–60); excludes bounce/return/reversal categories (line 16) |
| `PFMCategorization.py` | `pfm_categorization(transactions)` (line 8) | Maps category/subcategory/merchantType into PFM taxonomy: `pfmCategoryOne` (14–81), `pfmCategoryTwo` (83–191), `pfmCategoryType` EXPENSE/INCOME/TRANSFER (193–204) |
| `SimpleDescription.py` | `simple_description(transactions)` (line 6) | Builds `pfmSimpleDescription` = "PartyName - Category label" using enum display names |
| `RecurrentTxns.py` | `recurrent_transactions(transactions)` (line 8) | Groups txns by partyName Levenshtein clustering (`cut_tree`, height 1.5) into `Group_ID` |
| `AppUtil.py` | `clean_input_df` (6), `sep_by_*` splitters (14–45), `fuzzy_match` (48), `py_extract` (61) | Shared parsing/extraction helpers used by all bank scripts |
| `RegexConstants.py` (191 lines) | constants only | Cross-bank regex dictionaries: `SALARY` (6), `LOAN_REP`/`LOAN`/`LOAN_DESC` (9–14), `CREDIT_CARD` (20), `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` (86), `INSUFF_BOUNCE` (87), `SALARY_DISB` (88), `INTERNAL_PAY` (93), merchantType lists NBFC/HFC/INSTANT_LOAN (105–109), etc. |
| `BankRegexConstants.py` (432 lines) | constants only | Bank-specific extraction patterns, e.g. `SBI_CP_PATTERN*`, `SBI_AUTOPAY*`, `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*`, `HDFC_FT_PATTERN*`, `BANK_VER`, `BANK_CHARGES_HDFC` |
| `TransactionCategoryEnums.py` (170) / `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` (135) | `TransactionCategory`, `TransactionSubcategory` enums | Display-label mappings for categories and subcategories (used by SimpleDescription) |

## 3. Tests

**There are no test files in the repository.** I verified:
- No `test*`/`*test*` files exist anywhere (glob returned nothing)
- No references to `pytest`, `unittest`, or `nose` in any file
- No CI configuration, no test framework in `setup.py` dependencies
- The only test-related artifacts are commented-out dendrogram plotting blocks labeled "For testing purpose only" in `SalaryDetection.py` (lines 27–32) and `RecurrentTxns.py` (lines 16–21)

The only way to exercise the code is to run the service and POST to its endpoints, e.g.:
```
cd /app/categorizationapp && pip install -e .
gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app      # or docker build from /app
# then POST JSON to http://localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction
```

## Key takeaways
- The system is a rule-based (regex + pandas conditions) enrichment engine for Indian bank statements; there is no ML model despite sklearn being a dependency (scipy clustering is used for salary/recurrence grouping).
- Rule ordering matters everywhere: `np.select` takes the first matching condition, so reversal/bounce/cheque rules are placed before generic rail rules (UPI/NEFT/IMPS), with `TRANSFER` as the fallback category.
- The per-bank blocks in `Controller.py` are ~30 copies of an identical pipeline differing only in the categorizer function called — the shared logic lives in `UtilityScripts/`.

Done. Five one-token faults, each mapped to a forum complaint, fixed with no collateral movement.

## Root causes and fixes

**mango_saver — numeric-remark cheque deposit → generic transfer** (`BankScripts/HDFC.py:100`)
The rule required the remark to be exactly 15 chars long *and* match `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` (11 zeros + 5 digits = 16 chars minimum) — a self-contradiction, so the rule could never fire and rows fell to the `TRANSFER` default. Restored the regex to `^[0]{10}[0-9]{5}` (10 + 5 = 15), consistent with the length guard. Since the rule previously matched nothing, no other row can shift.

**mango_saver — bare-numeric salary credit lost its SALARY sub-tag** (`BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`)
The rule compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the canonical value everywhere else in the codebase (Controller.py, Purpose.py, InternalPayment.py, ICICI/SBI/Indusind scripts) is `"SAVING"` — a dead comparison. Fixed to `"SAVING"`.

**rk_ontheroad — leading direction-word transfers get empty/wrong counterparty** (`BankScripts/ICICI.py:159`)
`py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 0 — the direction word itself — instead of group 1, the name. "To" was then blanked by the later `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` cleanup (empty), while "From" survived (wrong). Fixed to `index=1`, matching the same idiom used correctly at ICICI.py:168.

**auditlens — slash-delimited 4-field bill transfer lifts the numeric reference** (`BankScripts/ICICI.py:147`)
For `BIL/INFT/<numeric ref>/<payee>` (exactly 3 slashes), the rule took field index 2 (the numeric reference) instead of the final field. Fixed to `sep_by_(...,3,4)`, consistent with the sibling rules at lines 148/154/206 that all pull the trailing payee field.

**maintainer — offsetting credit after matching debit labeled bounce, not reversal** (`BankScripts/HDFC.py:98`)
The pairwise reversal rule compared the credit's description with the row **two** back (`shift(periods=2)`) instead of the immediately preceding debit, so it never matched and the generic pair rule on line 99 claimed the row as `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`. Fixed to `shift(periods=1)` — identical to the correct twin rule in ICICI.py:49. Non-rail identical pairs still correctly resolve to `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` via line 99.

## Verification
- A synthetic harness reproducing each complaint row confirms all five now enrich correctly (REVERSAL, CHEQUE_DEPOSIT, SALARY, "John Doe"/"Jane Smith", "Acme Corp").
- A 216-row regression corpus (36 common HDFC/ICICI narration shapes × SAVING/CURRENT, run through the categorizer + `purpose` + `clean_names` pipeline) is byte-identical before and after the fixes — nothing that was already correct changed.
